rounds.text: Shilp Gravures Ltd trades at an exceptionally attractive valuation, offering a trailing P/E of 11x and a price-to-book ratio of just 0.80x against a book value of ₹ 176 per share [E1, E2]. This undervaluation is further highlighted by a compelling EV/EBITDA of 5.69x, representing a deep discount to the sector benchmark of 10.96x, alongside a price-to-book multiple that sits far below the sector benchmark of 5.05x [E7, E11]. Beneath these low multiples lies a fundamentally sound balance sheet, characterized by a negligible debt-to-equity ratio of 0.03x, robust short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 6.30x, and a status as almost debt-free [E36, E37, E48]. Operational quality is also turning a corner, as evidenced by expanding operating margins of 15% in the TTM compared to 13% three years earlier, and strong cash conversion of 1.37x with ₹ 9.59 Cr in operating cash flow fully backing reported profits for Mar 2026 [E29, E33, E34]. This momentum translates into explosive near-term profit growth, with compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months surging by 179% [E21]. conceded: [E42]

The company suffers from stagnant long-term fundamentals, highlighted by a compounded sales growth of just 4% over 10 years [E14] and 0% compounded profit growth over the last 5 years [E19]. Returns on capital are underwhelming, with an ROE of 7.9% [E13] and a 3-year median ROE of a meager 5% [E27]. Despite a low headline price-to-book ratio, a discounted cash flow valuation estimates intrinsic value at Rs 107 per share against a higher market price of Rs 141 [E42], resulting in a negative margin of safety of -32.3% [E43]. Furthermore, free cash flow has turned negative to Rs -7.76 Cr in March 2026 [E35], and borrowings have risen to Rs 3.59 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 0.29 Cr a year earlier [E38]. Conceded: the company trades at a low price-to-book ratio of 0.80x [E2] and maintains conservatively low debt-to-equity of 0.03x [E36].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over 10 years is 4% [E14] and compounded profit growth over 5 years is 0% [E19]. However, the bear overlooks that profitability has sharply inflected in the trailing twelve months with compounded profit growth hitting 179% [E21], while operating margins have expanded to 15% in the TTM from 13% three years earlier [E29]. Conceded: the 3-year median ROE is 5% [E27]. Nonetheless, the latest annual ROE reads higher at 8% [E28], demonstrating accelerating return metrics that align with positive screening signals showing sales up QoQ and expanding margins [E55, E56]. Addressing the balance sheet and cash flow concerns, the bear ignores that cash conversion is exceptionally strong at 1.37x with reported profits fully backed by cash [E33], operating cash flow reached Rs 9.59 Cr [E34], and the company remains exceptionally well-buffered with a negligible debt-to-equity ratio of 0.03x alongside a comfortable current ratio of 6.30x [E36, E37]. Finally, reliance on a DCF model yielding a negative margin of safety [E43] misses the profound discount offered by a price-to-book ratio of 0.80x [E2]—trading at a steep discount to the sector benchmark P/B of 5.05x [E7]—and an EV/EBITDA of 5.69x that sits roughly half of its sector benchmark of 10.96x [E11].

Conceded: compounded profit growth hit 179% in the trailing twelve months [E21], and cash conversion is 1.37x [E33]. However, citing this recent profit spike ignores the stagnant multi-year reality where 10-year profit growth is 4% [E18] and 5-year profit growth is 0% [E19]. The bull's focus on an 8% annual ROE [E28] glosses over the persistent mediocrity of a 3-year median ROE of just 5% [E27] and an overall ROE of 7.9% [E13] that lags the sector benchmark of 10.21% [E9]. Furthermore, while the debt-to-equity ratio remains low at 0.03x [E36], actual borrowings rose to Rs 3.59 Cr in September 2026 from just Rs 0.29 Cr a year earlier [E38], and free cash flow turned deeply negative at Rs -7.76 Cr in March 2026 [E35]. Finally, appealing to a low price-to-book ratio of 0.80x [E2] and an EV/EBITDA of 5.69x [E11] cannot override the disciplined DCF calculation showing intrinsic value at Rs 107 [E42] and a negative margin of safety of -32.3% [E43], confirming that the valuation is fundamentally unsupported by its low growth trajectory.
